items.title: [Twisted] Twisted: Unauthenticated Remote Denial of Service in the Twisted IRC Server via an Unbounded Line Buffer
items.summary: SummaryAn unbounded-buffer vulnerability (CWE-770) in the Twisted words IRC server lets any unauthenticated remote client exhaust server memory. twisted.words.protocols.irc.IRC.dataReceived appends every received byte to a per-connection buffer and only removes data at a line feed, with no maximum length. Because IRC is a plain Protocol and not a LineReceiver, one connection that streams bytes without a line feed grows the buffer without bound and drives the whole single-threaded process to out-of-memory, dropping every user at once. The twistd words server inherits the method unchanged through IRCUser, and the data is buffered before any authentication.DetailsIRC.dataReceived keeps everything up to the last line feed in self.buffer:# twisted/words/protocols/irc.pyclass IRC(protocol.Protocol):        # not a LineReceiver, so no MAX_LENGTH    buffer = ""    def dataReceived(self, data):        if isinstance(data, bytes):            data = data.decode("utf-8")        lines = (self.buffer + data).split(LF)        self.buffer = lines.pop()    # no 3line feed -> whole input stays buffered        ...With no line feed in the data, lines.pop() returns the entire accumulated content to self.buffer, so it grows by every chunk and is never bounded; IRC defines no MAX_LENGTH, no lineLengthExceeded, and no timeout, so the connection is never closed. The twistd words server protocol IRCUser subclasses IRC without overriding dataReceived, and the buffer is filled before any PASS, NICK, or USER, so no credentials are required.Affected product: Twisted (twisted.words), twisted.words.protocols.irc.IRC and its subclass twisted.words.service.IRCUserAffected versions: 26.4.0 and earlierPoCOn a standard Twisted words IRC server (the server twistd words runs, using IRCUser), an unauthenticated client opens a single TCP connection and continuously sends data that contains no line feed, never completing a line. Every chunk is appended to the connection's line buffer, and because no complete line is ever formed none of it is consumed, so the buffer grows by the full volume sent.In a measured run against a real IRCFactory server, one unauthenticated connection sending 60 MB of line-feed-free data raised the server process resident memory from about 47 MB to 2966 MB (roughly 49 MB per MB sent) with the connection still open and no limit triggered. Sending the same volume as normal line-feed-terminated commands leaves memory flat, which isolates the cause to the missing line-length bound.ImpactAn unauthenticated remote denial of service from allocation without limits (CWE-770) leading to uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-400). A single credential-free connection exhausts the memory of the whole twistd words process, and because one process serves every user, the crash drops all connections at once and the service stays down until it is restarted. The quadratic buffer copy reaches the same effect faster. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact and no code execution.Referenceshttps://github.com/twisted/twisted/security/advisories/GHSA-53xc-49m8-p798https://github.com/twisted/twisted/pull/12771https://github.com/twisted/twisted/commit/01f8cff7753c1edac132380b2ea939fa6bdbab30https://github.com/twisted/twisted/commit/ac90fb7b0ab73688a581fcd9a7c0577ec8ca3059https://github.com/twisted/twisted/releases/tag/twisted-26.10.0rc1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-53xc-49m8-p798

items.title: [Twisted] Twisted: Unauthenticated Remote Denial of Service in the Twisted conch Telnet Transport via an Unbounded Subnegotiation Buffer
items.summary: SummaryAn allocation-without-limits vulnerability (CWE-770) in the Twisted conch telnet transport lets any unauthenticated remote peer exhaust server memory over a single connection. When the peer opens a telnet subnegotiation with IAC SB and then streams bytes without ever sending the IAC SE terminator, every byte is appended to a per-connection buffer that has no maximum length. The buffer persists across reads and is released only on the terminator the attacker withholds, so it grows without bound until the process is killed.DetailsThe option-negotiation state machine in Telnet.dataReceived enters the subnegotiation state on IAC SB and sets an empty command list. In that state every non-IAC byte is appended to the list with no length check:# src/twisted/conch/telnet.py  (Telnet.dataReceived)elif self.state == "subnegotiation":    if b == IAC:        self.state = "subnegotiation-escaped"    else:        self.commands.append(b)      # unbounded: no len(self.commands) checkself.commands is an instance attribute that persists across dataReceived calls and is deleted only when IAC SE completes the subnegotiation. Negotiation runs at the transport layer before authentication, and the bytes are consumed inside dataReceived before any application callback, so an application cannot impose a bound. Twisted caps other parser buffers, for example NetstringReceiver.MAX_LENGTH, but not this one.Affected product: Twisted, twisted.conch.telnet transportAffected versions: confirmed against 26.4.0PoCOn any endpoint that exposes the Twisted telnet transport, such as the Twisted manhole telnet service, open one connection and send the two bytes IAC SB (0xFF 0xFA), then stream any non-0xFF bytes continuously and never send the IAC SE terminator (0xFF 0xF0). No credentials are required, because option negotiation runs before authentication.Every byte is appended to the per-connection subnegotiation buffer with no maximum, and the buffer is released only by the terminator the attacker withholds, so it grows for the life of the connection. Because each byte is retained as a separate element the memory consumed is several times the traffic sent, so a modest-bandwidth peer, or several such connections, drives the process to memory exhaustion.ImpactThis is an unauthenticated remote denial of service (CWE-770, CWE-400) by memory exhaustion. A single connection grows an in-memory buffer without bound at a cost proportional to the bytes sent, amplified by per-byte object overhead, until the operating system kills the server and every service it hosts. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact and no code execution. The affected surface is any deployment that exposes a Twisted telnet or manhole transport to untrusted peers.Referenceshttps://github.com/twisted/twisted/security/advisories/GHSA-cwm5-jh59-mwxrhttps://github.com/twisted/twisted/pull/12750https://github.com/twisted/twisted/commit/073ba878c6c07d569cb61abc5ae76d46eff1b529https://github.com/twisted/twisted/commit/5d91cc66a3591faba758a80a1479e0103602facchttps://github.com/twisted/twisted/releases/tag/twisted-26.10.0rc1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cwm5-jh59-mwxr

items.title: [Twisted] Twisted: Unauthenticated Remote Denial of Service in the Twisted words domish XML Element Stream via an Unbounded Element Tree
items.summary: SummaryAn allocation-without-limits vulnerability in the Twisted XML element stream lets any unauthenticated remote peer exhaust server memory over a single stream. When the peer opens a container element and streams child elements without ever closing the container, every element is materialised into an in-memory tree with no limit on depth or child count. An element is released only when its end tag arrives, so a container the attacker never closes retains everything beneath it until the process is killed.DetailsIn ExpatElementStream._onStartElement, each start tag appends a new element to the current element's children and descends into it, with no depth or child-count check:# src/twisted/words/xish/domish.py  (ExpatElementStream._onStartElement)if self.documentStarted == 1:    if self.currElem != None:        self.currElem.children.append(e)   # append child: no depth/count cap        e.parent = self.currElem    self.currElem = e                      # descend into the new elementAn element is emitted and dropped only when its end tag arrives while it sits directly under the document root, so a container that is never closed keeps every child beneath it. The transport XmlStream.dataReceived feeds bytes to self.stream.parse(data) with no size limit, and in XMPP the stream is parsed during negotiation before authentication.Affected product: Twisted, twisted.words.xish.domish element streamAffected versions: confirmed against 26.4.0PoCOn any endpoint that parses untrusted XML streams with this stack, such as an XMPP server, open a stream by sending the opening stream:stream tag and a container element, then stream child elements continuously and never send the container's closing tag. No credentials are required, because in XMPP the stream is parsed before authentication.Every child is appended to the container and retained because the container is never emitted, and the transport applies no limit on the size of the unfinished document. Because each small element becomes a full object in memory the footprint is many times the traffic sent, so a modest-bandwidth peer, or several such streams, drives the process to memory exhaustion.ImpactThis is an unauthenticated remote denial of service by memory exhaustion. A single stream grows an in-memory element tree without bound, amplified by per-element object overhead, until the operating system kills the server. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact and no code execution. The affected surface is any deployment that parses untrusted XML streams with this stack, such as an XMPP server or component.Referenceshttps://github.com/twisted/twisted/security/advisories/GHSA-3476-c5c2-fr73https://github.com/twisted/twisted/pull/12751https://github.com/twisted/twisted/commit/8873814bec8288e2466fad4d2c4d64039beb88b0https://github.com/twisted/twisted/releases/tag/twisted-26.10.0rc1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3476-c5c2-fr73

items.title: [Twisted] Twisted: HTTP Request Smuggling in twisted.web via a Bare CR or LF in a Header Value
items.summary:
SummaryAn incomplete header-value validation (CWE-444) in the Twisted HTTP server lets a bare carriage return or line feed in a header value hide a following header from the parser. twisted.web.http.HTTPChannel.headerReceived rejects a NUL byte in a header value but not a bare CR or LF, even though RFC 9110 section 5.5 requires a recipient to reject all three. Because the channel splits requests only on CRLF, a value carrying a bare LF and a second header arrives as one line, so the second header is folded into the value and the request is framed with no body. A front-end that treats the bare LF as a line terminator frames the request differently, and the disagreement lets an attacker smuggle a request past it. This is an incomplete fix of the earlier Twisted request-smuggling advisories, which guarded the NUL sibling of this exact check.DetailsheaderReceived splits a header line on the first colon, strips space and tab from the value, and validates it with a single test that rejects only NUL:# twisted/web/http.py  HTTPChannel.headerReceiveddata = data.strip(b" 	")if b"\x00" in data:          # NUL rejected; a bare CR or LF is not    self._respondToBadRequestAndDisconnect()    return FalseThe channel delimiter is CRLF, so Foo: x
Content-Length: 39 is one line: the split yields name Foo and value x
Content-Length: 39, strip leaves the LF, and the NUL check passes. _maybeChooseTransferDecoder is then called with Foo, never sees a Content-Length, and installs no body decoder, so the request is framed with an empty body. The header name and request line already reject CR and LF, so the value is the only gap.Affected product: Twisted, twisted.web.http.HTTPChannelAffected versions: 26.4.0 and earlierPoCFeed one connection a request whose header value carries a bare LF and a Content-Length, followed by a second request in the bytes after it: POST /public HTTP/1.1
Host: v
Foo: x
Content-Length: 44

GET /admin HTTP/1.1
Host: internal

. Twisted parses two requests and serves both, so the smuggled GET /admin returns the /admin response body even though the visible request was only POST /public. The bare CR variant behaves identically, and a NUL in the value is rejected, which isolates the missing CR and LF checks.Behind a front-end that treats the bare LF as a line terminator, the front-end frames one POST /public and forwards a body while Twisted frames a second GET /admin; the extra response then poisons the shared connection, so a later victim receives the attacker's GET /admin response.ImpactThis is an HTTP request-smuggling exposure (CWE-444) from inconsistent interpretation of a request (CWE-436). Through a front-end that accepts a bare CR or LF as a line terminator, an attacker can smuggle a request the front-end never sees, bypassing front-end access controls, poisoning a shared connection so a later victim receives the attacker's response, and poisoning a cache. Twisted is the strict endpoint that frames the request without a body, so it is realized only behind such a proxy, and there is no code execution.Referenceshttps://github.com/twisted/twisted/security/advisories/GHSA-q7qq-6mhp-9rc4https://github.com/twisted/twisted/pull/12755https://github.com/twisted/twisted/commit/022b6f7feb5980166c71f54e2c0d8f4f21ff6e1ahttps://github.com/twisted/twisted/commit/1616f702d36eda8990a5a5b22ad70fab140a7eb1https://github.com/twisted/twisted/releases/tag/twisted-26.10.0rc1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q7qq-6mhp-9rc4

items.title: [vllm] vLLM: Forged multimodal UUID + P0/P1 processor-cache eviction drift: unauthenticated remote crash of the whole vLLM engine
items.summary: SummaryMultimodal content parts (image_url, video_url, input_audio, ...) accept a user-supplied uuid field that vLLM uses verbatim as the item's cache identity (mm_hash). The two frontend/engine processor caches (P0 "sender" cache in the API process, P1 "receiver" cache in the EngineCore process) are independent LRU caches whose evictions are not synchronized, and the P1 hit path performs zero consistency validation — it silently substitutes the cached item's tensor data for whatever the current request actually contains.A single unauthenticated client can exploit this to kill the entire engine, deterministically, with default server flags:Seed: send a small image with uuid="U". Both caches now map U to an item with N_A visual tokens (e.g. 4).Drift: send ~70 requests, each carrying a unique uuid, a max-size image, and an over-long text prompt. Each request is rejected with 400 — but after its image has been inserted into the P0 cache (insertion happens during chat rendering, before prompt-length validation), so these requests fill P0 without ever reaching the engine/P1. U is evicted from P0 only.Kill: send a large image with uuid="U". P0 misses → the image is freshly processed and the prompt is spliced with N_B (e.g. 2048+) placeholder tokens; the request carries full data to the engine, but P1 still has U → the engine discards the fresh data and substitutes the stale N_A-row tensor. The scheduler plans for N_B encoder slots while the worker merges N_A embeddings into N_B placeholders → ValueError: Attempted to assign 4 = 4 multimodal tokens to 2048 placeholders at vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:711 → uncaught in the EngineCore busy loop → _send_engine_dead() → the EngineCore process dies, every API server reports EngineDeadError and shuts down. /health never recovers; the deployment needs a full restart.Verified end-to-end on the official vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0 image with Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, default configuration (no flags beyond --served-model-name/--gpu-memory-utilization): after 70 flood requests the kill request returned 500 EngineCore encountered an issue and /health went dead permanently. The vulnerable code is byte-identical on main (post-0.29.0).Details1. The client-controlled uuid becomes the cache hash verbatim. vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py:1677 / :1884-1886 read part["uuid"] per content part and pass it through as mm_uuids. In vllm/multimodal/processing/inputs.py:62-63, when no hf_processor_mm_kwargs are present (the default for chat requests), the uuid string is the item hash — no content binding at all:# vllm/multimodal/processing/inputs.py:62-63else:    hashes.append(uuid_item)        # client string used verbatim as mm_hash2. P0 insertion happens before request validation. In the serving path, render_chat_request (vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py:275) runs full mm processing — mm_processor.apply (vllm/renderers/base.py:759) → _cached_apply_hf_processor → _merge_mm_kwargs → cache.get_and_update_item (vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:1338), which inserts the processed item into the P0 sender cache (default mm_processor_cache_type="lru", 4 GiB). Only afterwards does get_max_tokens (vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/api_utils.py:183-186) reject over-long prompts with 400. A request can therefore write to P0 while never reaching the engine — the primitive that desynchronizes P0 from P1. (Public issue #43941 documented this same asymmetry for the opposite drift direction, which was later handled via MultiModalCacheMissError; the P0-miss/P1-hit direction below was never addressed.)3. P1 substitutes cached data on hash hit with no consistency check. In the EngineCore input thread, preprocess_add_request (vllm/v1/engine/core.py:997-1000) calls mm_receiver_cache.get_and_update_features, which only replaces feature.data (vllm/multimodal/cache.py:673-690) and keeps the request's own mm_position (placeholder layout). On a cache hit the receiver cache returns the stale item wholesale:# vllm/multimodal/cache.py:739-740  (MultiModalReceiverCache.get_and_update_item)if (cached_item := self._cache.get(mm_hash)) is not None:    return cached_item              # fresh data silently discarded; no size/modality checkOnly the opposite drift (P0 hit / P1 miss, data=None) is handled, via the retryable MultiModalCacheMissError. Nothing validates that the cached item's modality, shape, or token count matches the current request's placeholders.4. The mismatch is fatal to the engine. The scheduler plans encoder work from the request's (fresh) placeholder count N_B, while the worker gathers embeddings from the stale N_A-row tensor (encoder-cache hit under the same forged hash, or re-encoding the stale data — both yield N_A rows). _merge_multimodal_embeddings then raises:# vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:703-714inputs_embeds[is_multimodal] = mm_embeds_flat.to(dtype=input_dtype)   # RuntimeError...raise ValueError(    f"Attempted to assign {expr} = {num_actual_tokens} "    f"multimodal

items.title: [vllm] Duplicate Advisory: vLLM vulnerable to remote denial of service through forged multimodal UUID cache desynchronization
items.summary: Duplicate AdvisoryThis advisory has been withdrawn because it is a duplicate of GHSA-p92p-rxj5-7p2x. This link is maintained to preserve external references.Original DescriptionvLLM before 0.31.0 uses a client-supplied multimodal uuid verbatim as cache identity with no consistency check on cache hits, allowing engine crashes. Unauthenticated attackers can desynchronize the P0/P1 processor caches to trigger a fatal token-placeholder mismatch, killing the entire serving instance until restarted.Referenceshttps://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-p92p-rxj5-7p2xhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-114050https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/vllm-before-0.31.0-remote-engine-crash-via-forged-multimodal-uuidhttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hfwf-hgvp-4rr8

items.title: [brotli] Brotli: Out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder ("Node2Shell") also affects the PyPI Brotli package
items.summary: A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.Referenceshttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-111497https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases#nodejs-brotli-decoder-out-of-bounds-write-permits-remote-code-execution-cve-2026-111497---highhttps://github.com/google/brotli/commit/0ed4268a4401abcb4472096340477cf4af7d1a2bhttps://github.com/google/brotli/commit/50a9b70a4d5e1443fc40927952276b68fffa83a0https://github.com/google/brotli/commit/b418fa81c48262a86a95332b0bc6d62c30aa78b6https://github.com/google/brotli/commit/da9806362874b9bd4b552a3af360b5d6347beb12https://github.com/google/brotli/releases/tag/v1.0.10https://github.com/google/brotli/releases/tag/v1.1.1https://github.com/google/brotli/releases/tag/v1.2.1https://github.com/pypa/advisory-database/tree/main/vulns/brotli/PYSEC-2026-4322.yamlhttps://github.com/pypa/advisory-database/tree/main/vulns/brotlicffi/PYSEC-2026-4323.yamlhttps://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releaseshttps://opensourcemalware.com/blog/node2shell-affects-pythonhttps://pypi.org/project/Brotlihttps://pypi.org/project/brotlicffihttps://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-111497https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35
